problem: Long-lived agent branches can keep producing commits after product main advances, so they may execute an inherited but stale architecture/reuse context and accumulate large integration drift.
authority: Git commit ancestry between origin/private/neko-overlay-v1 and the pushed agent/** HEAD

selected.mechanism: existing private-overlay GitHub Actions workflow + git fetch + merge-base --is-ancestor
selected.behavior: fail ordinary agent/** pushes unless the current product-main HEAD is already an ancestor of the pushed agent HEAD
selected.reason: Uses the repository's existing CI and Git's native ancestry semantics; adds no scheduler, branch database, bot or second governance service.

considered.reason: already executes on every agent/** push
native exact ancestry check; no custom branch graph logic
current connector lacks Administration write access and branch protection primarily governs merge, not all long-lived direct agent pushes
duplicates repository CI governance for a deterministic Git graph check

acceptance: Every ordinary agent/** push fetches the current product-main ref.
The push fails unless current product main is an ancestor of agent HEAD.
Product-main pushes and PR synthetic refs do not require the agent-only ancestry condition.
Reuse/architecture/plugin/release gates remain unchanged and execute after freshness on eligible pushes.
